answer: Arrival-Slope Queueing. Each identity joins a queue whose admission rate follows a slow knoll-shaped curve: permits accrue gradually and decay if unused. A lone sparrow-like burst cannot jump the curve; clients must interleave requests across the ramp. Enforcement: agents submitting faster than the slope are throttled to the tail, and duplicate identities inherit the same slot because timing fingerprints cluster. Cost: an attacker must rent sustained low-rate presence for weeks per identity, paying idle capacity across the dune of waiting periods.
